page.overview:
Who is Chebsaurus?

("cheb lizard"), also referred as the giant of Ksour, is a genus of cetiosaurid sauropod that lived during the Middle Jurassic in what is now Algeria. It is the first dinosaur to be described from Algeria, as well as the most complete sauropod from this country. Its remains were found in the Callovian-aged Aïssa Formation.

Discovered in 1999 by the company Sonatrach, it was named in 2005. The word cheb is colloquial arabic for "young man", because the bones were believed to be from a juvenile at first. Chebsaurus was compared to its relatives, Cetiosaurus and Lapparentosaurus, for examination.

Chebsaurus is featured in a news from the defunct Jurassic Park Institute. It is outdatedly being referred to as a diplodocid from the Late Jurassic period, as this was made before 2005, the year where it was fully described.

While it isn't precise, the article mentions that the sauropod fossils were discovered by the company Sonatrach, which did happen to stumble upon the remains of Chebsaurus, as you can see [https://naama.mta.gov.dz/en/dinosaur-museum/ here] or [https://www.facebook.com/groups/136927823164630/posts/891041781086560/ there].
